data.long_meaning: The name Jorim is derived from the Hebrew language, meaning 'God is my light'. This name reflects the belief in God as the source of illumination and guidance, especially in times of darkness and uncertainty.

historical_references.reference: Jorim, son of Jeshunah, was a prominent Levite during the time of King Hezekiah. He played a crucial role in the restoration of the Temple and the reinstitution of the sacrificial system. (2 Chronicles 29:10)

Jorim is also mentioned as the father of King Josiah of Judah in 2 Chronicles 34:1. Josiah ruled during the late 7th and early 6th century BC and is notable for his religious reforms and efforts to restore the Temple.
